newsitem.title: USA: US senator has bill to auction TV channels.
newsitem.headline: US senator has bill to auction TV channels.

text.p: The head of the Senate Commerce Committee said Monday he will introduce legislation to auction six of the TV channels 60-69 for alternative uses while allocating the remaining four channels for law enforcement and public safety organziations.
Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, said auction proceeds could be used for deficit reduction.

McCain said the reallocation of the four channels for public-safety purposes would be made possible through the transition to high-definition digital TV. That transition will free up existing channels for alternative uses.

The bill, to be offered Tuesday, also would require the government to auction six more channels with the provision that 10 percent of all revenues derived from the auction would be earmarked for distribution to the states.

The money would be used to purchase services and communications equipment for public safety radio users. McCain said the sum of these revenues would be a minimum of $200 million and could exceed $750 million.
